questions.question: Driving a combination vehicle ____ than driving a single vehicle.
questions.correctAnswerText: Requires more driving skill
questions.explanation: Driving a combination vehicle requires more skill than driving a single vehicle. Combination vehicles are longer and heavier.

questions.question: Rollovers happen when drivers:
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn too quickly
questions.explanation: A rollover happens when a driver takes a turn too fast. Always take turns and curves slowly and carefully.

questions.question: What does the trailer air supply control look like?

options.text: It is a square blue knob
It is a triangular yellow knob
It is an eight-sided red knob
It is a circular orange knob

questions.correctAnswerText: It is an eight-sided red knob
questions.explanation: The trailer air supply control on newer vehicles is an eight-sided red knob. It controls the tractor protection valve.

questions.question: Pull out the trailer air supply control to test:
questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer emergency brakes
questions.explanation: Test the trailer emergency brakes before starting a trip. After checking that the trailer rolls freely, pull out the trailer air supply control to test the emergency brakes. Pull forward slightly with the tractor. The trailer should not move.

questions.question: After connecting the air lines to the trailer while coupling, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Supply air to the trailer
questions.explanation: Following the correct steps to couple and uncouple trailers is important for safe operation of combination vehicles. After connecting the air lines to the trailer, supply air to the trailer.

questions.question: Avoid needing to make sudden lane changes by:

options.text: Using your horn to encourage other drivers to move out of your lane
Only driving slower than the posted speed limit
Watching the road ahead while driving
Pulling off the road and waiting when there is heavy traffic

questions.correctAnswerText: Watching the road ahead while driving
questions.explanation: Sudden lane changes are dangerous when driving a combination vehicle. Avoid sudden lane changes by looking ahead for obstacles that will require you to change lanes.

questions.question: The emergency air line:

options.text: Is controlled by the foot brake
Is connected to the relay valves
Supplies air to the trailer air tanks

questions.correctAnswerText: Supplies air to the trailer air tanks
questions.explanation: The emergency air line (also called the supply line) has two jobs. It supplies air to the trailer air tanks and controls the emergency brakes.

questions.question: What is off-tracking?

options.text: When a vehicle's front wheels follow a different path than its rear wheels
When a vehicle's wheels all follow the same path
When a load shifts during a turn
When a vehicle's wheels run over a curb during a turn

questions.correctAnswerText: When a vehicle's front wheels follow a different path than its rear wheels
questions.explanation: When a vehicle turns a corner, the rear wheels follow a different path than the front wheels. This is called off-tracking.

questions.question: A trailer will swing around most likely when:
questions.correctAnswerText: It is empty
questions.explanation: An empty trailer needs a longer stopping distance than a loaded trailer. An empty or lightly loaded trailer is most likely to swing out and hit other vehicles.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve:

options.text: Should always be used for parking
Should only be used for parking on a downhill
Should never be used for parking
Should only be used when transporting cargo

questions.correctAnswerText: Should never be used for parking
questions.explanation: Do not use the trailer hand valve for parking. It can cause air to leak from the braking system, which could release the brakes. Use the parking brake instead.

questions.question: When inspecting a coupling, you should go under the trailer and:

options.text: Detach the jaws from the kingpin.
Make sure the locking lever is in the emergency position.
Look into the back of the fifth wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look into the back of the fifth wheel.
questions.explanation: When inspecting a coupling, go under the trailer and look into the back of the fifth wheel. Check that the fifth wheel jaws are wrapped around the kingpin shank.

questions.question: What happens when a trailer's wheels lock up?

options.text: The trailer usually continues to move in a straight line.
The trailer will likely swing around.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer will likely swing around.
questions.explanation: When a trailer's wheels lock up, it tends to swing around. This can cause a trailer jackknife.

questions.question: After finishing a pre-trip inspection, you should:

options.text: Leave the rear shut-off valves open.
Leave the emergency line valve open.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the emergency line valve.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, open the rear emergency and service line shut-off valves to check that air reaches all brakes. You will hear escaping air. Close both valves before you start driving.

questions.question: Proper coupling technique:

options.text: Is the same on all vehicles.
Is essential to safe vehicle operation.
Includes making sure the fifth wheel plate is not greased.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is essential to safe vehicle operation.
questions.explanation: Learning proper coupling and uncoupling is critical to safely operating combination vehicles. Improper coupling is very dangerous.

questions.question: If the fifth wheel plate is not properly greased, it could:
questions.correctAnswerText: Cause steering problems.
questions.explanation: A fifth wheel plate that is not properly greased creates friction between the tractor and trailer. This causes steering problems.

questions.question: If a trailer begins to skid, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Release the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your trailer skids while braking, release the brakes. The wheels will regain grip on the road. Once they do, the trailer will straighten out and follow the tractor.

questions.question: If you need to back your trailer but cannot back in a straight line, you should:

options.text: Swerve back and forth while backing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back toward the driver's side.
questions.explanation: If you must back your trailer on a curve, back toward the driver's side. This gives you the best visibility while backing.

questions.question: If your trailer goes off course while backing, you should:

options.text: Pull forward, readjust, and start backing again.
Get out and move the trailer into position.
Turn the steering wheel all the way left until the trailer straightens out.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward, readjust, and start backing again.
questions.explanation: If your trailer goes off course while backing, pull your truck forward to reposition your vehicle. Then continue backing.

questions.question: Changing lanes quickly can cause:

options.text: A crack-the-whip effect that can cause a rollover.
Confusion about which lane the driver wants to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: A crack-the-whip effect that can cause a rollover.
questions.explanation: The crack-the-whip effect in combination vehicles causes the rear to move more than the front. Changing lanes too quickly can cause a rollover.

questions.question: In a double or triple combination, where should the heaviest trailer be?

options.text: Cargo weight must be evenly distributed between all trailers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Directly behind the cab.
questions.explanation: The heaviest trailer should be closest to the tractor. The lightest trailer should be in the rear.
